industry: Homeowners, condo and renters insurance (agents, agencies, carriers; flood/earthquake add-ons)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'Covers everything' / 'full protection' / 'are you sure you're covered for everything?' styled as a promise (policies cover named or covered perils; carriers' own guides ban implying everything is covered).
'Save up to X%' or recipient-specific savings estimates (gold 016's '$1,027' street-view estimate) unless calculated from real data and substantiated.

'ATTENTION: your homeowner's policy is about to renew!' (gold 005) or variable-data 'your policy will renew on [date]' (gold 013) unless you actually have that data lawfully; otherwise it implies a notice from their insurer.
House-on-fire or disaster imagery used without a clear protective step (EPPM backfire), or real disaster victims' homes without permission.
'Flood covered' or 'earthquake covered' unless the specific policy covers it.
Unsourced statistics; FEMA/NFIP or government logos implying affiliation (39 USC 3001(h); state unfair trade practices).
Unaudited vendor results quoted as fact.
compliance_notes: State unfair trade practices acts (NAIC Model 880) bar misrepresenting policy benefits/terms and false advertising; inducements follow the 2020 anti-rebating amendment as adopted by each state.
Producer licensing disclosure: CA Ins. Code 1725.5 license number on print ads in CA (size rules) plus the word 'Insurance'.
Savings claims require substantiation (FTC Sec. 5); describe as averages among customers who saved, with basis.
NFIP flood policies generally take effect after 30 days (exceptions for mortgage-related purchases and certain map changes) - state the wait accurately if used as urgency.
Rebuild-cost reviews: don't promise a specific replacement-cost outcome; some states (e.g., CA, CO) have specific replacement-cost estimate/offer rules - check before claiming.

Realtor co-branded cards (gold 018) can trigger RESPA Section 8 issues if referral fees/things of value flow between agent and insurer in a mortgage transaction (noted in NAIC 880 drafting note; not researched further).
Testimonials real and typical (16 CFR 255); claim stories need the customer's permission.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, status, relief, nostalgia are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle and combo carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency/vendor-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.
No age/demographic angle unless a cited source supports it for this industry; even then, check Fair Housing / ECOA before using it in housing or credit.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold house-on-fire 'Are you sure your insurance covers everything?' (003) vs misrepresentation rules and EPPM
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law and verified studies win: keep the fear, drop 'everything', add one doable step (rebuild check). Fire imagery is allowed but warm-home imagery with a sourced line is preferred.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold variable-data 'your policy will renew on January 1st' (013) / 'about to renew' (005) vs state unfair trade practices
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: use only real, lawfully held renewal data; otherwise 'Renewal coming up?'.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold 001 targeted 'younger homeowners' vs standing rule on age angles
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Standing rule wins: no age message; life-event timing (new purchase) instead. Age as a list filter is a client decision, but avoid it in housing-adjacent contexts without legal review.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Progressive guide avoids fear imagery for home vs Patrick's emotion-agnostic rule
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Patrick's rule wins (brand choice, not law); fear OK when true and paired with an action.
